section.title: De-hyphenation and re-tokenizing term vectors
section.para: DehyphenationCharSequenceNormalizer joins words split at a line break, such as "litiga-\ntion" to "litigation". A letter, optionally followed by combining marks, must precede the hyphen, and a letter must follow the break. Spaces between the hyphen and the break, which PDF and OCR output often leaves, and the indentation of the next line are deleted with the hyphen, so "litiga- \n tion" becomes "litigation" as well. The supported hyphens are U+002D, the soft hyphen U+00AD, U+2010, and the hyphens other scripts use at a line end: U+058A (Armenian), U+1400 (Canadian syllabics), U+2E17 (Fraktur) and U+10EAD (Yezidi). Dashes, the non-breaking hyphen U+2011, and the hyphens that join compounds or names, such as the Hebrew maqaf U+05BE and U+30A0, are excluded.

Breaks use UnicodeWhitespace.lineBreaks(): U+000A, U+000B, U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. CRLF counts as one break. The set is wider than StringUtil.isLineTerminator: word processors export a manual line break as a vertical tab, and PDF text extraction writes a form feed at a page end. Additional breaks prevent a join, so "litiga-

TION", joins. The soft hyphen marks a break inside one word, so it joins before a capital as well. Han, Hiragana, Katakana and Hangul text breaks lines between characters without hyphenation, so a hyphen next to a letter of these scripts is kept. No dictionary is used: a lower-case compound split at a hyphen, such as "well-
known", becomes "wellknown".

In a TextNormalizer pipeline, add the de-hyphenation step first. whitespace() turns the line break into a space, stripInvisible() deletes the soft hyphen, and dashes() and nfkc() turn the non-breaking hyphen into a hyphen that would then join.

opennlp.tools.dehyphenation.RetokenizingTermVectorAnnotator tokenizes normalized text and groups terms in tokenizer output order. Unlike TermVectorAnnotator, it does not use an existing token layer, so a joined word can become a single term. Existing layers and document text are preserved. Empty token spans are omitted in both modes. Full mode includes original-text occurrence spans; scoring-only mode includes counts without spans. Offsets use UTF-16 code units.
